t: Genghis Khan founded Karakorum in 1220 in a valley that earlier Xiongnu, Göktürk and Uyghur empires had used, and under Ögedei from 1235 it became a walled capital with a fixed palace.
It was the capital of the Mongol Empire until 1260, when the empire divided and Khubilai Khan made Dadu the seat of the Yuan dynasty, leaving Karakorum an administrative centre.
Ming armies occupied it in 1372 and 1380, and in 1585 its stones and bricks went into the Erdene Zuu Monastery; its site was identified in 1889.
dyk: A large tree of silver and other precious metals stood in the courtyard of the Khan's palace, with four golden serpents round the trunk and a mechanical angel that sounded a trumpet when drinks were wanted. It was designed by Guillaume Boucher, an enslaved Parisian goldsmith.
ev: The foundation of Karakorum is usually dated to this year
Ögedei Khan decrees the Palace of Myriad Peace and has city walls built
The Mongol Empire divides and Khubilai Khan develops Dadu as the capital of the Yuan Empire
Lingbei Province is founded and Karakorum remains the administrative centre north of the Gobi
A Ming army under Li Wenzhong occupies the city and causes severe damage
Abtai Sain Khan founds the Erdene Zuu Monastery on the palace site, using stones and bricks of Karakorum
Nikolai Yadrintsev identifies the ruins as the Mongol capital

f.founded: Genghis Khan rallied his troops at a place called Karakorum in 1218 and 1219, and the foundation of the city is usually said to have occurred in 1220. His successor Ögedei built city walls and a fixed palace from 1235.
f.where: In the upper Orkhon Valley, in the north-western corner of the Övörkhangai Province of Mongolia, near the present town of Kharkhorin.
f.known: Capital of the Mongol Empire from 1235 to 1260; the Palace of Myriad Peace; the Silver Tree of Guillaume Boucher; the account of William of Rubruck, who reached it in 1254; the great stupa temple; the Erdene Zuu Monastery built from its stones
f.today: The ruins lie beside the Erdene Zuu Monastery in the upper part of the Orkhon Valley World Heritage Site, near the town of Kharkhorin.
